questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city Prague, because of it's beauty and geographic location in the middle of Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it okay, some good powerpoints with information that was usefull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved information from the International Office, and attended the online meeting and the introduction day. I met with my buddy a few days after arrival, and he was a great help and friend throughout me entire stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fine for me, I found it some months in advance, so I had good time. I found mine through a Facebook group, and stayed in an apartment with 4 others. We rented an apartment through Erasmus In Prague. The apartment was very nice and had a great location. The communication with the company was not great.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it can be difficult to communicate with the companies if any problems accurs. Be determined and make sure that you dobble check your contract.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not like the dorms, and I am happy that I did not choose to live there after I saw them.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing to enroll for the courses, and the website SIS is really old. I was very stressed about the process, but ended up getting courses I liked - I heard from fellow students at Charles that I was lucky. The International Office at the faculty of Social Science is amazing, all very sweet and helpfull. So I did not feel left alone with the difficulties.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found a lot of courses that I wanted, and was ready at the exact time when they opened for enrollment. Many of my wishes did not exist for some reason, so I had to stress find a lot of courses and enroll for a lot that I did not want. Ended on a lot of waiting lists, and in the end I ended up with some nice courses. But it was difficult to make the 30 credits on point!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international Office, and they are so kind and helpfull - a great experience!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Many of the courses I originally wanted did not exist in the end, but i managed to find other interesting ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready at the exact time for enrollment! The spots disspear very fast. And expect to make a lot of changes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To of my courses wer great and very interesting (Contemporary social Theory and Medical Anthropology). My last two courses very not great (Anthropology of EU and Urban Anthropology). I expected a lot from the two last ones, but sadly the Professor did not at all manage to make it interesting or understandable. It was very confusing and the level of english was not great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level in Contemporary social Theory and Medical Anthropology was great, and I learned a lot! Great with seminars and student presentations, that involved us and created great discussions. The level in Anthropology of EU and Urban Anthropology was not great, the professors level in english was not great, and therefore it was not always easy to follow him. There was a general lack of context, and I never really understood where the lections were going.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I missed having seminars where I could discuss and talk to my fellow students about the readings. Also, The professor in Anthropology of EU and Urban Anthropology did not engage with us at all, which was also a shame.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Anthropology of EU and Urban Anthropology, Contemporary social Theory and Medical Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contemporary social Theory and Medical Anthropology. Great courses with participation and interesting readings! Not too much work, but enough to also process and understand the themes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I regeral, you just end up spending a lot of money on traveling. I traveled around the country, and also to other European countries. This was a really great experience, so be ready to spend a little more than you expect!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks (ecspecially beer) was way less expencive than expected. Public transportation was also very cheap if you buy a student transportation card.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not participate in a lot of these, so I don't know a lot about it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some cultural workshops and sometimes some social activities from the social clubs at the faculties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the social activities arranged by the social clubs. The Manifesto marked and the events there are great! They have nothing to do with the university, but all the Erasmus students go there, and you meet a lot of new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around the country and see Bohemian Paradise, Brno and so on. Visit other great cities close, like Budapest and Krakow. Explore the many great food places in Prague! And Manifesto marked in the beginning, to meet new people. And also, go to Dog Bar!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not find it difficult. Czech people can be a bit grumpy and introvert, but get used to this. A bit difficult with the language sometimes, but most often it was not a problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a buddy!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The grumpyness of Czech people. Not always very service minded.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved trying Czech food, going to the park and going for walks in the city and the beer culture of course.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get ready for a bit confusing and challenging enrollment process, where you have to make a lot of changes. But this will work out in the end, and after this, Prague is a perfect city to be an Erasmus student in! The best way to explore Prague is to just walk around the city, it is beautiful. Get at student transportation card and enjoy the trams. Enjoy the cheap prices, and make sure to participate in a lot of social activities in the beginning like Manifesto marked and other events - then you are secured a lot of new friends and amazing times.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The enrollment system, and also, a great idea to attend some of the classes before choosing - I should have done that

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses, because I was a bit dissapointed in two of them. Also the communication with our landlord, which was a bit challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
